records.name: Global Philadelphia Association
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings together Philadelphia's international community. It runs a World Heritage City project, a global directory, a program for emerging international journalists, and a young professionals network.
records.what_you_do: Attend the public talks, artist panels, and town halls the group hosts, or join its Young Professionals Network. Internship and volunteer openings are listed on the site.

schedule.text: Public events are listed on the homepage with their own dates. No weekly or monthly meeting is shown.

locations.label: Office
locations.address: Two Logan Square, 100 to 120 N 18th St, Suite 530

cost.text: Event prices and membership dues are not listed on the homepage.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter from the site footer, then come to the next public event you can make.
first_step.basis: Public events are open to anyone, and the site has a clear sign up path for news and membership.

records.notes: Newest dated item is a news post dated October 5, 2026. The homepage shows every event date as October 8, 2026, which looks like a display date, so those dates were not used. Membership, internship and contact pages were linked from the homepage but not read. Email is behind the contact page, so none is recorded. IRS legal name: Global Philadelphia Association Inc.

records.name: Great Dames
records.summary: A network for women that runs peer advisory groups, a members' circle, and grant programs for women's ideas. Members meet, learn together and support each other.
records.what_you_do: Join the members' circle, attend listed events such as the virtual pitch event, or ask through the contact page about other ways to take part.

schedule.text: Events are listed on the site by date, but the pages read showed no dates for the peer groups or the virtual pitch event.

cost.text: Membership fees and event prices are not shown on the pages read.

first_step.how: Use the join link on greatdames.com to look at the members' circle, or attend a listed event.
first_step.basis: Most events are open to anyone, and the site has a clear join link, though fees are not shown.

records.notes: The Philadelphia link is weak. Neither page names a city, a chapter or a meeting place, so please check whether this should show as a Philadelphia group. The Queen Street address comes from the IRS filing only. Newest dated item is news from November 20, 2025. Contact details are not on the pages read; the contact page was not opened. IRS legal name: Great Dames Fund Inc.

records.name: Hairs 2 U Wig Bank
records.summary: A nonprofit wig shop in Queen Village. It gives wigs to people who have lost their hair to illness, and it sells wigs and head coverings to everyone else.
records.what_you_do: Book a free consultation to be fitted for a wig or learn wig care, or shop in person. The free wig program ships wigs to people who qualify. Donations keep the free program running.

schedule.text: The site does not publish regular hours. A 2020 article said appointments can be set before or after normal hours. Book a consultation to confirm a time.

cost.text: Wigs in the free program are listed at $1 each, plus shipping. Shop wigs are sold at regular prices.

first_step.how: Book a consultation at hairs2u.org/consultations. For the free wig program, ask your hospital doctor or social worker to complete the program's patient form first.
first_step.basis: The shop and consultations are open to anyone, but the free wig program needs a form signed by a hospital doctor or social worker.

records.notes: The IRS filing's web address field held an email address, so the group's site was found through a January 2020 Inquirer article that links hairs2u.org. The site's newest dated item is a 2025 Wig Walk that was postponed to spring with no date given; the 2024 copyright is not counted, so no month is recorded and status is probably_active. The IRS address (616 S 4th St) is on South 4th Street, the street the 2020 article says the group left in 2016; no current street address was found, so none is recorded. The email hairs2uwb@yahoo.com comes from the IRS filing, not the group's site; confirm before relying on it. IRS legal name: Hairs 2 U Wig Bank.

records.name: HealthLink International
records.summary: A nonprofit institute that runs health and technology training, including biomedical equipment repair, pharmacy services, and nursing assistant courses. It also builds links between schools and partners abroad for exchanges and study trips.
records.what_you_do: Ask about one of the training programs: management information systems technician, biomedical equipment repair, pharmacy services, or community health education technician with nursing assistant. Students and career changers can also ask about exchanges.

schedule.text: Class dates and times are not listed on the pages read. Ask the group for the next start date.

cost.text: Program fees are not listed on the pages read.

first_step.how: Call 215-521-1900 or use the contact page to ask about the next start date for the training program that fits you.
first_step.basis: Training programs usually need an application, and the site does not explain how to apply or start.

records.notes: No dated news or events. The footer year (2019) and photo file names (2006 to 2011) are not counted, so status rests on a working site with no dates. Physical class location is not published; the only address is the PO Box. IRS legal name includes Gci Inc.

records.name: Kingdom and Community Connections
records.summary: A faith-based service ministry that offers counseling, mentoring, job skills training, money training, and parenting workshops. The site says people can come whether or not they attend church.
records.what_you_do: Join a program such as the men's coaching group, the mentoring program for young women, financial freedom training, or employment skills help. The group also runs a meal assistance program and makes referrals to other agencies.

schedule.text: Program times are not listed on the site. Call or email to ask when each group meets.

cost.text: Program fees are not listed on the site.

first_step.basis: The site does not describe a sign-up or intake step, so the way in is unclear.

Its work is statewide, not a Philadelphia meeting place. The page gives no address, email, phone, or any way for the public to join or volunteer, so hidden as private. records.name: LiveWell Foundation
records.summary: A peer-led, volunteer-run nonprofit for people living with depression. It runs free online support groups, workshops, and public events, and it lists groups for the Philadelphia area.
records.what_you_do: Join a free online peer support group for adults, people in recovery, teens, or seniors, or come to a public talk or workshop. Volunteers and partners can use the Partner and Volunteer page on the site.

schedule.text: Group times are published on the site, but the page read did not show dates or times.

cost.text: Online peer support groups are free. Therapy and coaching with LiveWell clinicians are paid.

first_step.how: Pick a free online peer support group from the site (adults in English or Spanish, people in recovery, teens 14 to 18, or seniors 65 and up), or email contact@livewell-foundation.org to ask about Philadelphia-area groups.
first_step.basis: Groups are free and open to the public, and each one is listed by who it is for, with a clear way to join.

records.notes: The site lists a BIG Talk event and Philly Groups without dates, so status rests on a working site with no dates. The site says LiveWell does not provide emergency services and gives crisis lines; those were not copied here. Legal status is not stated on the site; the IRS lists it as a nonprofit. Philly Groups list is a lead for future research.

records.name: Londonzo
records.summary: A community movement led by its members. It runs a speaker and mentor program focused on violence prevention and youth leadership, and it asks people to help with drives and events.
records.what_you_do: Email the group to volunteer, help plan an event, host a sneaker drive, or ask about the speaker and mentor program. Donations and merchandise purchases are optional ways to support the work.

schedule.text: No dates or meeting times are listed on the site.

cost.text: Volunteering is free. Donations and merchandise are optional.

first_step.how: Email londonzo2020inc@gmail.com and ask about volunteer roles or the speaker program.
first_step.basis: The site lists volunteer and speaker options but gives no sign-up steps or meeting details.

records.notes: The blog link has no posts, and the only year on the site is a 2021 copyright, which is not counted; status rests on a working site with no dates. The site shows no address or phone. The IRS filing address is 709 N 2nd St Ste 400, 19123, but the site does not confirm it, so it is not recorded. The site sells merchandise and does not say whether it is a registered nonprofit. IRS legal name: Londonzo Inc.

Hope on Girard: the search found no organization by that name, so its record is unknown and should be held back. Hairs 2 U: a 2020 Inquirer article linked the group's own site, which was then read. Connection refused (mpcfund, irug) and certificate expired (lwci) were each retried once and are listed in blocked; none was a rate limit across many domains.
